what: `blaze cache gc --dry-run` is not read-only: it takes each area's collector lock and writes its own name into .blaze-collector (and, since this lane's change, makes a lease in a lease-less build dir). A lane told to run only read-only commands cannot use it on a home it may not modify.
cost: the per-verdict counts of the tracked objects were taken from --last instead
cause: a dry run shares the real run's locking
whys: collector_lock writes the holder's name on taking the lock
a dry run takes the same lock as a run that removes
prevention: none yet: a dry run could plan under a shared lock and write nothing
